metaTitle: Free Electrician Invoice Template — No Signup, No Watermark
metaDescription: Free electrician invoice template for licensed electricians and contractors — no signup, no watermark. Download an editable Word and PDF invoice or make one online.
intro: This is a free electrician invoice template made for licensed electricians, electrical contractors, and apprentices who bill for service calls, wiring jobs, and repairs. It gives you clear lines for labor hours, parts, and a service call fee, plus room for your license number, so a homeowner or general contractor sees exactly what they are paying for.

It is completely free, with no signup and no watermark. Download the editable Word and PDF files and fill them in on your own computer, or use the generator below to build your invoice in the browser and download a print-ready PDF in minutes.
included: A line for your service call or trip fee, plus labor lines for hours worked at your hourly rate
Separate line items for parts and materials — breakers, outlets, wire, fixtures — with quantity and unit price
A header for your business name, logo, address, contact details, and electrician license number, and a section for the client you are billing
A unique invoice number with issue and due dates so each job is easy to track and reference
Automatic subtotal, tax, and grand total, plus a notes and payment-terms area for deposits or Net 30
Free editable Word and PDF files, print-ready on one page, with no watermark and no signup

steps.title: Add your business, license, and client details
steps.body: Enter your company name, logo, contact info, and electrician license number at the top, then add the customer and the service address. Give the invoice a unique number and set the issue and due dates.

steps.title: List your service fee, labor, and parts
steps.body: Add a line for the service call or trip fee, then labor by hours at your rate, and each part or material as its own line with quantity and price. The template totals the line items, adds tax, and shows the grand total for you.

steps.title: Download and send
steps.body: Download a print-ready PDF (or the editable Word file) and email it to the homeowner, property manager, or general contractor. Include your payment terms — a deposit, due on receipt, or Net 30 — and how you want to be paid.

faqs.q: How do I bill a service call fee and labor on the same electrician invoice?
faqs.a: Put the service call or trip fee on its own line, then add your labor as a separate line with the hours worked and your hourly rate. List any parts or materials below that as their own lines. The template adds every line into one subtotal, applies tax, and shows a single grand total, so the customer sees both the total and the breakdown behind it.

faqs.q: Should I put my electrician license number on the invoice?
faqs.a: Yes. Most states license electricians, and many homeowners and general contractors expect to see your license number on the paperwork. The template has a header field for it next to your business name and contact details, which also helps with permits and inspections.

faqs.q: Do I charge sales tax on an electrician invoice?
faqs.a: It depends on your state and the work. U.S. sales tax rules for electrical contractors vary — some states tax the parts and materials, some tax the full labor-and-materials job, and some treat the contractor as the end user of materials. The template has a tax line that calculates automatically; set the rate that applies to you, and check your state's rules if you are unsure.

faqs.q: Is the template really free with no watermark?
faqs.a: Yes. The Word and PDF files are free to download and use, with no signup and no watermark. You can reuse them for every service call and job and edit them however you like.
